title: Inventory rounding decisions
scenario: Ruvella Parts Depot is planning stock for 30 fictitious items. Demand is in units, while replenishment uses complete packs; stock can contain a partial pack. Unit costs include extra decimal places so the invoice policy can round each line to cents.

lesson.intro: Changing number format only changes display. Rounding changes the calculated value. Enter the first row formula and fill down so relative row references move to the next item.

functions.name: ROUND
functions.purpose: Round to the nearest stated decimal position.
functions.arguments: number is the input; num_digits is decimal places, 0 for an integer or negative for tens/hundreds.
functions.useCase: Round monetary line values to cents.
functions.mistake: Formatting as currency is not mathematical rounding.

functions.name: ROUNDUP
functions.arguments: number is the value; num_digits sets the retained decimal position.
functions.useCase: Order enough complete packs for positive demand.
functions.mistake: Up means away from zero, including for negative numbers.

functions.name: ROUNDDOWN
functions.arguments: number supplies the input; num_digits controls the retained decimal position.
functions.useCase: Count complete packs in positive stock.
functions.mistake: Down means toward zero; it is not the mathematical floor for negatives.

lesson.combine: Reuse SUM after rounding each line if the policy rounds lines individually. Rounding the grand total can differ. Data!B2/Data!D2 moves to row 3 when copied; fix references only when the same constant must be used in every row.

tasks.prompt: Round the first item’s Unit_cost_CAD to two decimal places.
For the first five items, calculate the number of complete packs to order to meet Demand_units. Return one integer per row in dataset order.
For the first five items, calculate complete packs contained in Stock_units. Ignore any incomplete remainder. Return integers in dataset order.
For the first five items, calculate Stock_units times Unit_cost_CAD, rounding each item value to two decimal places. Return values in dataset order.

bonus.prompt: Total the five individually rounded stock values from task 4. Round that total to two decimal places.

columns.name: Stock_units
columns.description: Physical stock on hand, including partial packs.

columns.name: Pack_size_units
columns.description: Positive units supplied per complete pack.

columns.name: Unit_cost_CAD
columns.description: Cost per unit in Canadian dollars, three decimal places.
